finding: PCL directory is currently an uninitialized subfolder inside a user home-directory git repository (C:/Users/91961).
evidence: Command `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` returned `C:/Users/91961` with user home directory tracked files.
impact: If pushed directly from the parent git context, unrelated private personal files from C:/Users/91961 could be exposed.
recommended_action: Initialize a clean standalone Git repository inside the PCL root directory (`git init`) before pushing to GitHub.

finding: Open-source license has not been formally approved by the Project Director.
evidence: README.md notes license selection is pending director decision; docs/OPEN_SOURCE_TODO.md lists Apache 2.0 / MIT as options.
impact: Publishing without an explicit license creates legal ambiguity regarding copyright and commercial usage rights.
recommended_action: Project Director formally approves Apache 2.0 or MIT license and commits the standard LICENSE file.

finding: Security vulnerability contact email is currently a placeholder notice.
evidence: SECURITY.md specifies 'The project director will designate the official private security contact email'.
impact: External security researchers finding cryptographic or parsing vulnerabilities would have to disclose via public issues or maintainer DMs.
recommended_action: Project Director designates an official security intake address (e.g., security@pcl.dev or GitHub Private Vulnerability Reporting).

finding: Domain vocabulary URIs (e.g. https://pcl.dev/vocab/logistics/v0) are illustrative test URIs and not yet live web endpoints.
evidence: Spec notes that PCL core does not dereference vocabulary URIs at runtime.
impact: External developers attempting to fetch vocabulary URIs via HTTP GET will receive 404 until static hosting is deployed.
recommended_action: Ensure documentation explicitly states that vocabulary URIs serve as global unique string identifiers, with static web landing pages planned for future hosting.

finding: Cryptographic test vectors contain RFC 8032 deterministic test private key seeds.
evidence: spec/test-vectors/evidence-vectors.json explicitly tags seed with NON-SECRET RFC 8032 TEST SEED notice.
impact: Safe for public release because test keys are standard public RFC vectors and not production operational keys.
recommended_action: Maintain explicit non-secret notice in test vector documentation.
